apps.localizedDescription: The iPhone remote for Control Center: see every task's status, answer questions, approve plans and start tasks on your Mac.

versions.localizedDescription:
## What's new

### Planning
- **Approving the repos starts planning.** When `/analyze-task` proposes repos and you approve them, a feature switches to plan mode at once. A bug finds the root cause first, then switches to plan mode by itself. Tasks that only need a reply are unaffected. Settings → Defaults → "Plan after approving repos".
- **Plan mode runs research without asking.** Plan mode used to ask before every shell command. Now commands, searches and sub-agents run straight through, and you're only asked before a file is edited. Settings → Defaults → "In plan mode" also offers "Allow everything" or "Ask for each tool". The plan itself and Claude's questions always come to you.
- **Comment on parts of a plan.** Select text in a plan and use "Comment on selection" (or right-click). On the iPhone, long-press a part of the plan. Your comments go back to Claude as quoted remarks, together with any general feedback.

### Pull requests
- **Failing CI is fixed automatically.** Once all checks on one of your PRs have finished and a required one failed, Claude gets the failed logs, fixes and pushes. If the failure isn't the PR's fault (flaky, infrastructure), the failed jobs are re-run once; if they fail again, the task needs you. Failing optional checks are left alone. Settings → Automated review fixes.
- **Drafted answers to review comments from people.** For each new comment, Claude prepares a fix (committed locally) or a reply, and nothing is pushed or posted yet. The drafts appear on the task, on the Mac and the iPhone: edit the replies, skip any, then Send. Skipped fixes are dropped, approved ones pushed, replies posted, and threads that got a fix are resolved. A reviewer's follow-up in a thread you already answered counts as new. Review bots aren't treated as people.
- Failing checks now say which checks, on which PR, and whether they are required.
- Tasks remember the PRs they opened, so merged work shows Merged.

### Digest
- **What changed since you last looked.** Come back after a few hours away and a digest opens: what needs you, review replies to approve, failing checks, merged PRs, auto-fixes, finished tasks and errors. It's also in the toolbar and the Task menu.
- **Morning digest.** A short summary is pushed to your iPhone through ntfy at a time you choose (8:30 on weekdays by default). Tapping it opens the digest on the phone. Without ntfy it is a Mac notification. Settings → Notifications → Digest.

### Tasks
- Tasks stay where you put them: drag to reorder. Sub-tasks can be collapsed under their parent, in the list and on the board.
- Archiving a task archives its sub-tasks too, and stops its processes and containers. A week later its worktrees and volumes are removed; unarchiving brings them back.
- Sub-sessions wake their parent when they finish, and the parent's card shows them live.
- **Esc stops Claude** and puts messages Claude hadn't started on back in the reply box.
- Claude's replies, questions and plans are one selectable text on the Mac, so a selection can span the whole message. Whole replies can be copied.

### Reliability
- Claude is never left waiting for background jobs that were stopped.
- Shell commands end when their process exits, even if something they started keeps running.
- Claude talking about rate limiting is no longer mistaken for a usage limit.
- No more "Thinking…" after a turn that had already read a queued message.

## What's new

### Send images and files to Claude
- **Images:** paste a screenshot (⌘V), drag images onto the chat, or use the paperclip. On the iPhone, the + menu has Photo Library, Take Photo and Paste Image. Claude receives the image itself, the same way the terminal sends a pasted screenshot. Large images are shrunk to 2000 px.
- **Any file:** logs, PDFs, CSVs, specs and code work the same way: paste, drag or pick them on the Mac, or "Choose File" on the iPhone. Control Center keeps a copy, tells Claude where it is, and Claude can read it in every permission mode without a prompt. A pasted folder goes in as its path.
- **In the chat:** images show as thumbnails and files as chips with name, type and size. Click either to open it; the iPhone uses Quick Look.
- **New Task** accepts images and files on both the Mac and the iPhone, so a task can start from a screenshot or a document.
- **Terminal sessions** that contain pasted screenshots now show those messages with their images.

### Typing
- **Return sends** and **Shift+Return adds a new line** at the cursor, everywhere you write to Claude: the reply box, New Task, plan feedback, "Other…" answers and quick-action arguments. ⌘Return also sends. While Japanese or other input methods are composing, Return confirms the characters instead of sending.

### Clearer statuses
- **Needs you** now appears only when Claude is waiting on you: a question, a permission prompt, a plan to approve, a repo proposal, Claude reporting that it is blocked, or a reply that ends with a question.
- **Done:** a turn that ends with an answer or a progress report.
- **Paused:** tasks interrupted by an app restart or quit, a terminal handoff, or the Stop button. Paused tasks don't count toward Needs you.
- The summary Claude writes for itself when it compacts a long conversation is no longer shown as if you had typed it. A small "Conversation compacted" divider marks the spot.

### Review fixes stay with the work
- Automatic review fixes go to the task that opened the PR, matched by its PR or by the branch in any of its worktrees, so a task with PRs in several repos keeps all of them.
- If that task is busy, the fix waits for the next check instead of opening a new task. Archived tasks are brought back and used, and a worktree for the PR's repo is added when needed.
- PRs opened outside the app get one "Review fixes" task per branch, not one per PR. Existing duplicates are merged into it once they're idle; the duplicates are archived, not deleted.
- Task cards and the task header show every PR linked to the task.

### Reliability
- **No crash when changing the permission mode** from the task header, in single or split panes. An unexpected error no longer closes the app.
- **No more Settings crash** when deleting a quick action or a repository.
- **Messages sent while Claude is busy are never lost:** they're queued, labelled "Queued" in the chat, and sent again after a worktree move or account switch.
- **No orphaned sessions:** Claude sessions stop when Control Center quits or crashes, and leftovers are cleaned up at launch.
- **Terminal handoff:**
  - Replying in the app (after a confirmation) ends the terminal's session and continues here.
  - Stop ends the terminal session too.
  - "Show terminal" opens the exact Terminal or iTerm2 tab.
- **Plans:** you can approve a plan with "Yes, bypass permissions". In plan mode, repos are chosen on the plan card.

- Themes: Glass, Terminal and Plain
- Editable keyboard shortcuts
- Import: list only interactive terminal sessions, read just the start of each file
- Terminal: pick your terminal app; sessions continued there mirror live into the app
- Split chats: drag task cards into panes, resizable, remembered across restarts

- Mac .dmg releases with in-app updates, iPhone via SideStore; done stays done
- Stop the repeated Keychain password prompt
- Question card: don't repeat a preview the question already contains
- Never ask to approve a draft the user can't see
- Questions as buttons, readable plans, reliable status and Stop
- Repos are proposed by Claude after a first look, then approved
- Projects & lazy worktrees in <root>/<project>/<repo>/<task>
- Shift+Tab permission modes, quick actions never land in the wrong repo, iPhone navigation
- iPhone: persist pairing explicitly so it survives reinstalls
- Phone notifications: clarify they are Control Center events only; no duplicates
- Notifications: guided ntfy setup with subscribe QR, auto topic, test with delivery status
- aico via claude.ai connector (OAuth), iPhone over LAN + installer, adaptive board
- iPhone remote, e2e driver, newest-claude resolution, unattended auto-fix, UI polish
